references.text: Continues the account of how the Lord gave victory over Sihon and his people, showing the extent of the conquest
Similar wording stating that the Lord gave King Og of Bashan into Israel's hand, following the same pattern of divine surrender
The parallel account in Numbers regarding the battle against Sihon, where Israel struck him with the sword
Same language about the Lord giving the enemy into Israel's hand, and they struck him, his sons, and all his people
The Lord promises to deliver the nations into Israel's hands, reflecting the same theological theme of divine surrender for victory
Similar wording where the Lord gives a city and its king into Israel's hand during Joshua's conquest
Rahab confesses that the Lord has given the land into Israel's hand, echoing the same theme of divine surrender
The psalm praises God for the victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites, citing this as an example of God's mighty deeds
